cultural.vision_reason: A carved wooden harp with a skin-membraned soundbox, carved anthropomorphic head, and cane-strung pegs, attributed by the museum to the Ngbaka — a well-known harp-making people of Central Africa; matches claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: harp
physical.summary: Harp made of wood with a rectangular-faced wood sound box, rounded beneath. Skin membrane secured by cane pins. Two circular sound holes at opposing top and bottom corners. Sound box surmounted by carved wood head into which is fixed curved wood neck. Carved head decorated with brass tacks. Five peg holes; four pegs remain bound with cane strings. Two of strings are still attached to wooden string bar which is inserted into skin membrane.

cultural.vision_reason: A bow harp with carved human-head finial, skin-covered resonator, and traditional pegs/strings — a classic Central African harp type well documented among Ngbaka and neighboring peoples of the region, museum records maker as Ngbaka.

physical.title: harp
physical.summary: Bow-shaped harp made of wood with resonator topped by a carved human head and terminating in pair of stylised legs. Resonator has skin-covered top secured to wood frame with cane pins. Wood string bar inserted centrally with three twisted cotton strings attached, though broken. Patch of skin pinned over circular sound hole ? on resonator. Neck has five peg holes, three remaining wood pegs and part of fourth, fifth peg is missing. Pegs forked at one side, bound with cane and fibre strings attached.
